summary: Korean stocks are in a rout. The KOSPI fell about 6% on Oct 13 and broke below 6,000, after a 3.65% drop on Oct 12, and it is far below its June peak above 9,000. SK Hynix fell about 8.5% and Samsung about 6.8% as foreigners kept selling, on fears that China's CXMT will add server memory and end the shortage. Rising US borrowing costs add to the pressure. The Bank of Korea raised its rate to 3.0% in August and meets again Oct 22. Samsung and SK Hynix have no regular US listing, so US investors reach this mostly through EWY, Korean bank ADRs and Coupang.
for_you: Korea is a memory chip market, and memory is breaking down. Skip MU and memory swings until the selling stops. Avoid new buys in Korean bank ADRs before the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

changes.what: The KOSPI fell 2.62% to about 6,626 as foreigners kept selling Samsung and SK Hynix, each down about 2.4%. Profit taking in memory chips is driving Korea lower.

The KOSPI fell 3.65% to 6,384.24, its lowest close since Aug 11, as foreigners sold a net 2.02 trillion won for a tenth straight day. Samsung fell 4.39% and SK Hynix 4.52%, and China's CXMT said a new memory platform is in mass production.
changes.for_you: No action. Korean bank ADRs fall with foreign outflows; avoid new buys before the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision. The same memory selloff hit MU premarket, so skip memory swings for now.

changes.what: The KOSPI fell about 6% on Oct 13, below 6,000 for the first time since August, and a sell sidecar paused program selling. SK Hynix fell about 8.5% and Samsung about 6.8%, with SK Square down about 12%.
changes.for_you: No action except to stay out. EWY fell 4% Monday and has more to digest; MU is not a setup. Watch the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.
